localAgencies.notes: Issues PSD, minor NSR, nonattainment NSR, and Title V for its facilities (per EPA).

overview: Washington splits air permitting among Ecology, seven local clean air agencies, EFSEC (large energy facilities), and EPA Region 10 (Indian Country and the Outer Continental Shelf). Ecology issues permits in counties without a local agency and for pulp mills, aluminum mills, and Hanford statewide, and it issues all PSD permits not under EFSEC, EPA, or tribal jurisdiction. Before installing or modifying a source, a business needs a Notice of Construction (NOC) order of approval unless exempt under WAC 173-400-110; toxic air pollutant emitters may need a health impact assessment (WAC 173-460). General orders cover common source types. Major sources need an Air Operating Permit (Title V, WAC 173-401). Most permitted industrial sources must also join the registration program and pay annual fees.

permitTypes.name: NOC exemptions
permitTypes.description: Whether an NOC is needed depends on the equipment or its emission levels; exemptions and exemption levels are in WAC 173-400-110.

permitTypes.name: Registration program
permitTypes.description: Most companies with an industrial air permit must register and pay a yearly fee based on permitted emissions.

permitTypes.name: General Orders of Approval
permitTypes.description: Ecology general orders for asphalt plants, auto body shops, concrete batch plants, small perchloroethylene dry cleaners, rock crushers, and small water heaters and steam-generating boilers (in Ecology-jurisdiction counties). Portable plants with a valid local agency permit notify Ecology at least 15 days before working in an Ecology county.
permitTypes.thresholds: Dry cleaners using less than 2,100 gallons of perchloroethylene per year (restated from Ecology).

permitTypes.name: Notice of Construction (NOC) Order of Approval
permitTypes.description: Pre-construction permit required before installing or modifying an air pollution source (new businesses, replacing or changing control equipment, or increasing emissions). May require a SEPA checklist and a health impact assessment for toxic air pollutants. Ecology charges hourly or complexity-based fees (hourly rate $141 for 2026).

permitTypes.name: Prevention of Significant Deterioration (PSD)
permitTypes.description: For new large facilities or changes at existing large facilities that could increase air pollution. Ecology issues PSD permits statewide except for projects regulated by EFSEC, EPA, or tribes.

permitTypes.name: Nonattainment NSR
permitTypes.description: Issued by Ecology or the local clean air agency with jurisdiction (per EPA).

permitTypes.name: Air Operating Permit (AOP)
permitTypes.description: Apply 12 months before the business has the potential to emit the threshold amounts; renewals 6 to 18 months before expiration; 5-year term. Businesses below thresholds may still need an AOP under federal NSPS/NESHAP. Fees based on emissions and permit category.
permitTypes.quote: A business must complete an air operating permit application 12 months before the business has the potential to emit more than: 100 tons per year of any air pollutant. 10 tons per year of any hazardous air pollutant. 25 tons per year of a combination of hazardous air pollutants.

oilAndGas.summary: Washington has no meaningful oil and gas production program in Ecology's air permitting pages. Refineries and large energy facilities are handled through NOC/AOP permits by the local agency, Ecology, or EFSEC.
